chunks: Three narrators - My father (may Allah be pleased with him) said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated from al-Qasim ibn Muhammad al-Isfahani, from al-Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, from al-Hafs ibn Ghiyath al-Nakha'i al-Qadi, who said: I asked Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him),
about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High: ("But when his Lord manifested His Glory to the mountain He made it crumble"),
But when his Lord manifested His Glory to the mountain He made it crumble
He (peace be upon him) explained: "The Mountain slipped into the ocean, and is still sinking/grieving to this date."
ai.seo_question: What happened to the mountain after it crumbled when Moses saw God's glory?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Tawhid*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) interprets the phrase 'made it dust' (jadalah dakka) in Surah Al-A'raf not merely as a temporary crumbling, but as a continuous sinking or subsiding of the mountain into the sea. This explanation highlights the enduring nature of divine manifestation (Tajalli) on creation, suggesting that the physical effect of God's glory on the mountain persists until the Day of Judgment, offering a unique perspective on the permanence of divine attributes in the material world.

en.sayed-ali-raza-rizvi: 23. My father (RA) said: Sa`d ibn `Abd Allah said on the authority of al-Qasim ibn Muhammad alIsfahani, on the authority of Sulayman ibn Dawud al-Minqari, on the authority of Hafs ibn Ghiyath alNakha`I al-Qadi that I asked Abu `Abd Allah al-Sadiq (AS)
about the Word of Allah, the Mighty and High:
But when his Lord manifested His Glory to the mountain He made it crumble.6
He (AS) explained: “The Mountain slipped into the ocean, and is still grieving to this date.”
